title: KnOTS aligned LoRA Mirror bank
hypothesis: After shared orthogonal alignment, sparse task-coordinate codes preserve heterogeneous low-rank updates at lower complete bytes than native aligned cores and independent LoRA factors, beyond gauge-only effects.
physical_object: shared LoRA update subspace estimated from development tasks
mirror_coordinate: sparse aligned core code per task, with optional paid private rank-1 residual
controls: shared basis plus private rank-1 residual

development.selection_metric: held-out task-delta NRMSE, complete serialized bytes, gauge invariance

fresh.reason: mechanism screen only; audit not opened after development failure

success_gate: Held-out update NRMSE <=0.05 and >=25% complete payload savings against independent LoRA and native dense aligned cores, with native sparse controls not matching exactly.
failure_gate: Quality/byte gate miss, exact alias to native aligned code, or zero function diversity after gauge refactorization => FAIL for Mirror-specific value.
boundaries: Synthetic matrices only; no trained natural task adapters or base model.
Oracle held-out task updates measure representation only, not adaptation or task quality.
No fresh/audit, language or production runtime claim.
